## Historical audit — S0201

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/smoke/smoke_02/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines; supplied observations are complete lines, not split observations.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The explicit goal was to reconstruct a 170 × 256 indoor photograph with separate meshes and matching camera, materials and framing. The reference image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response and execute, lines 3–4 | The student interpreted the scene as a reading corner and programmed walls, window, multipart chair, ottoman, rug, books, hat, throw and curtains. It specified procedural upholstery, an angled camera and two lights. These are modeled intentions, not verification that the objects or their connections match the photograph. |
| Execution result, line 5; next request and response, lines 6 and 8–9 | Step 1 failed before rendering: the chair arm-front fillet radius exceeded half its smallest dimension. The runner supplied the traceback to the student; the revised program reduced that radius from .10 to .075 and was executed. |
| Execution result, line 10; next request and response, lines 11 and 13–14 | Step 2 advanced past that error but failed because the Blender world was `None`. The runner supplied this traceback; the student added conditional world creation, revised rug and upholstery details, and changed the camera from lens 45 to 58 and one light’s power from 100 to 120. The revised program was executed. |
| Execution result, line 15 | Step 3 timed out after approximately 526 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image. The timeout’s cause is not established. |

**Outcome and validation.** The observed outcome is two program execution failures followed by a technical interruption; no successful build or rendered image is recorded. The first correction is supported by the second execution reaching a later failure. The world fix’s effectiveness remains unknown. There is no independent visual or geometric verification of object count, materials, contacts between chair parts or objects, pose, occlusion, camera match, or lighting. The programmed hat tilt and book rotations establish intended poses only. No rendered comparison or formal success is visible.

**Input and exploration.** No teacher intervention is recorded: the two inputs after execution were runner error reports, not teacher diagnoses or visual advice. Their receipt is explicit in the subsequent student requests, and corresponding code changes show adoption. The student independently authored and revised the scene, including aesthetic changes without an available rendered view; the sessions report no tool events (lines 2, 7 and 12).

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, runtime tracebacks can localize construction constraints and missing environment state, but passing one failure does not validate the whole scene. Here, the particular fillet and world fixes are task-specific. Whether scene complexity contributed to the final timeout, whether the world fix worked, and whether any modeled appearance or placement resembled the unseen reference remain unresolved hypotheses.
